cases.note: The loop visits units in the same descending order (PB, TB, GB, MB, KB) with identical thresholds, breaks on the first match exactly like the else-if chain, and defaults to 'B' when no threshold is met. Every input selects the same unit as before, so this is an equivalent refactor with no observable behaviour change.

The patched explicit-integer pattern makes the sign mandatory for octal literals, so `!!int 0o777` (previously 511) now throws 'cannot resolve a node with !<tag:yaml.org,2002:int> explicit tag', while the implicit pattern and signed forms still work — an observable regression in the default core schema.

cases.note: Hoisting digits.slice(2) into a variable computed before the prefix checks is side-effect-free; it is only consumed in the same 0b/0o/0x branches where it equals the original value.slice(2), and the decimal fallback path is identical, so all inputs resolve identically.

Replacing 'type === string' with 'true' removes the type guard, so non-string values with a truthy length (arrays, {length:n}, functions) are coerced via String() and parsed instead of throwing the documented error. ms(['100']) now returns 100 (and ms({length:1}) returns undefined) where the original build threw.
